title: Independent 10 percent edge loss removes about 29 percent of timing constraints in selected Allen mouse slice graphs
abstract: We tested the loss of graph support for additive source-cell plus target-cell delay models in Allen Synaptic Physiology r2.1. We reproduced 18 independent constraints and 57 supported mouse edges, and one constraint with four human edges. Exact enumeration of all edge subsets in each cycle core shows that independent 10 percent edge loss leaves 12.8385 mouse constraints and 41.7211 supported mouse edges on average. This removes 28.67 percent of constraints while 90 percent of edges remain on average. Removing one cycle edge removes all constraints in its group for 28 of 57 supported mouse edges. Strict cell labels give 11 initial mouse constraints and 7.5161 after the same assumed loss. The human rectangle survives with probability 0.6561. These are exact conditional sensitivity results, not estimates of error rates or biological synapse loss. Small selected slice graphs, fixed connection calls, unmeasured correlated failures, and one human supported group limit inference. The package preserves code, source hashes, extracted edges, integer reliability coefficients, deletion audits, figures, and offline reproduction instructions.

display.caption: Exact expected retained constraints and cycle-supported edges under independent edge loss. The loss rate is assumed, not measured.
